title: Tens of Thousands March Across Portugal in Largest Protest Yet Against Housing Costs
dek: Demonstrators in more than 30 cities and towns demanded rent caps and tenant protections as home prices and rents rise faster than incomes.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Protesters at a housing demonstration in Lisbon’s Rossio square
image.credit: Afonso Dimas Martins via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Tens of thousands of people marched in more than 30 cities and towns across Portugal on Saturday, in what the Associated Press called the largest protest yet against soaring housing costs.

Activists want ceilings on rent increases, greater legal protection for tenants against eviction, and more affordable housing. Al Jazeera reported that the protests follow parliament's approval of government changes that make rental contracts more flexible and speed up evictions, which housing campaigners warned could weaken tenant protections.
Riot police with dogs have dispersed some protests, drawing accusations of heavy-handed tactics, AP reported.
Eurostat data cited by AP shows Portugal posted the biggest rise in the EU in the home price-to-income ratio between 2015 and 2025, at 61%.
body:
Tens of thousands of people marched through more than 30 cities and towns across Portugal on Saturday, in the largest demonstration yet against housing costs that many say have put buying or renting a home out of reach, [the Associated Press reported](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/tens-thousands-march-portuguese-cities-surging-home-prices-138144512).

## Where and who

[Al Jazeera reported](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/11/14/tens-of-thousands-march-in-latest-portugal-housing-protests) that the demonstrations were organised by the Casa Para Viver (A Home to Live In) platform and took place in Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Portimão, Coimbra, Braga and other locations. AP reported that participants ranged from teenagers to retirees, and that marchers carried banners under the slogan “We won’t let them steal our right to housing.”

## The crackdown and the camps

AP reported that the housing crisis has fuelled weeks of demonstrations, and that some activists have camped in central squares in Lisbon and Porto, the country’s two largest cities. Riot police with dogs have dispersed some protests, AP reported, drawing accusations of heavy-handed tactics.

## Why people are marching

AP reported that house prices in Portugal have risen much faster than incomes. Eurostat said Portugal posted the biggest rise in the EU in the home price-to-income ratio between 2015 and 2025, up 61%. AP also cited the National Statistics Institute, which said housing prices rose by almost 20% between the first quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026.

AP quoted a 35-year-old data analyst who works part-time as an astrologer to help pay her mortgage, and who said she worried about whether her younger sister could afford to move out of their parents’ home. Another marcher, 42-year-old Ana Encarnação, told AP that things had become “intolerable,” citing rising living costs and the widening gap between rich and poor.

## Origins of the protests

AP reported that the protests took inspiration from demonstrations that began in neighbouring Spain last month over similar housing concerns, and that they come amid widespread social unrest across Europe this autumn. Meridian has not independently verified the protest attendance figures, which are described in the reporting as tens of thousands.
